verdict.rationale: Stripe ships an official, agent-oriented CLI. The Link CLI gives agents wallet access, one-time-use payment credentials and permissioned financial data, and it exposes its own docs to agents via `link-cli --llms-full`. Its open-source repo is on GitHub, a runtime probe confirms it is published on npm, and the Stripe CLI is documented for coding agents to provision sandboxes. Missing for 10: independent hands-on or community corroboration of the CLI working in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: Link CLI gives your agent access to a wallet that your customer controls. Your agent can retrieve one-time-use payment credentials to complete purchases
Your agent can inspect the full CLI documentation with `link-cli --llms-full`
is published on the public npm registry (npm view @stripe/link-cli → 0.19.2; source at github.com/stripe/link-cli)
Coding agents should install the Stripe CLI (`npm i -g @stripe/cli`) and run the command `stripe sandbox create --help` to provision an anonymous Stripe sandbox with working API keys.
